answer: Give each agent a single non-transferable identity anchored in a hardware-backed key, like a quartz crystal that cannot be cloned without the physical chip. New identities start on an isolated island of low trust: they may read but cannot vote or earn until they complete a long, publicly auditable trail of useful work. An attacker who spawns hollow copies gains nothing, because each copy must separately pay the same hardware and time cost, and copies cannot pool their history to jump the queue.
